mishnayos.summary: On Chol HaMoed we may water a dry field that needs water, but not in a way that is very hard work.

chunks.en: We may water a thirsty field on Chol HaMoed and in the Shemittah year,
chunks.st: One may irrigate a field that requires irrigation on the intermediate days of a Festival as well as during the Sabbatical Year,

words.note: A dry field that is ruined if it is not watered often.
The in-between days of Pesach and Sukkos.
Shemittah, when fields in Eretz Yisrael rest.

chunks.en: both from a brand-new spring
chunks.st: both from a newly emerged spring that began to flow only during the Festival,

chunks.en: and from a spring that was already flowing.
chunks.st: and from a spring that did not just emerge and that has been flowing for some time.

chunks.en: But we may not water a field
chunks.st: However, one may not irrigate a field

chunks.en: with rainwater stored in a pit,
chunks.explain: Drawing it up is very hard work.
chunks.st: with rainwater
chunks.stMore: collected in a cistern, a procedure that requires excessive exertion,

chunks.en: or with water pulled up with a kilon.
chunks.st: or with water drawn with a shadoof [kilon],
chunks.stMore: a lever used to raise water with a bucket from deep down in a well.

words.note: A long pole with a bucket for lifting water from a deep well.

chunks.en: And we may not dig round ditches around grapevines.
chunks.st: And one may not construct circular ditches around the bases of grapevines on the intermediate days of a Festival.

words.note: Little circles dug around a plant's roots to hold water.

mishnayos.summary: Can we dig a new water channel on Chol HaMoed or in Shemittah? We may also fix things the public needs, like roads and mikvaos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: We may not dig a new water channel
chunks.st: One may not construct a new water channel

words.note: A ditch that carries water to a field.

chunks.en: for the first time on Chol HaMoed or in Shemittah.
chunks.st: during the intermediate days of a Festival or during the Sabbatical Year.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: We may dig a new water channel in Shemittah,
chunks.st: One may construct a new water channel during the Sabbatical Year

chunks.en: and we may fix broken channels on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: and one may repair damaged water channels during the intermediate days of a Festival.
chunks.stMore: In addition to performing labor on one’s own property in order to avoid financial loss, it is also permitted to perform labor on the intermediate days of a Festival for the public welfare:

chunks.en: We may fix broken water pits
chunks.st: One may repair damaged water cisterns

chunks.en: that belong to the public, and clean them out.
chunks.st: that are in the public domain, and clean them out by removing the dirt and sediment that accumulated there;

chunks.en: We may fix the roads,
chunks.st: one may repair roads,

chunks.en: the streets, and the mikvaos,
chunks.st: streets, and ritual baths;

words.note: Mikvaos are pools for becoming tahor (pure).

chunks.en: and take care of everything the public needs.
chunks.st: and one may tend to all other public needs.

chunks.en: We may mark the graves,
chunks.explain: So people know to stay away and not become tamei.
chunks.st: So too, one may mark graves to inform the public of their ritual impurity,

chunks.en: and messengers may even go out to pull up kilayim.
chunks.st: and inspectors may even go out to uproot the shoots of prohibited diverse kinds [kilayim] that grew in the fields during the rainy season.

words.note: Mixed plantings that the Torah forbids.

mishnayos.summary: May we bring water to trees and plants on Chol HaMoed? Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov allows only what is needed, and the Sages allow both.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: We may lead water from one tree to another tree,
chunks.st: In a field that is filled with trees, one may draw water via channels from one tree to another tree on the intermediate days of a Festival
chunks.stMore: because trees are in dire need of water.

chunks.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁקֶה אֶת כָּל הַשָּׂדֶה.
chunks.en: as long as he does not water the whole field.
chunks.st: And this is permitted provided that in doing so he does not water the entire field.

chunks.en: Plants that were not watered before Yom Tov,
chunks.st: With regard to plants that were not watered prior to the Festival,

chunks.en: he may not water them on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.explain: Because they don't really need it.
chunks.st: one may not water them on the intermediate days of the Festival
chunks.stMore: because they do not need the water.

chunks.en: But the Sages allow both.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis permit watering in this case, i.e., trees, and that case, i.e., plants.

mishnayos.summary: We may trap moles and mice that ruin fields, and close a gap in a garden wall on Chol HaMoed.

chunks.en: We may trap moles and mice
chunks.st: One may trap moles [ishut] and mice

words.note: Small animals that dig under fields and ruin them.

chunks.en: in an orchard and in a grain field,
chunks.st: in an orchard and in a field of grain

words.note: Literally a white field: an open field with no trees.

chunks.en: but not in the usual way,
chunks.explain: For example, by poking a stick into the ground instead of digging.
chunks.st: in a way that is not his usual manner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., as he would trap them all year round,

chunks.en: on Chol HaMoed and in Shemittah.
chunks.st: both on the intermediate days of a Festival and during the Sabbatical Year.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: In an orchard, in the usual way,
chunks.explain: Losing trees is a big loss.
chunks.st: In an orchard he may trap them in his usual manner,

chunks.en: but in a grain field, not in the usual way.
chunks.st: but in a field of grain, where there is no danger of substantial financial loss, he may only trap them in a way that is not his usual manner.

chunks.en: We may close a gap in a garden wall on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: And one may seal a breach in the wall of his garden on the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: and in Shemittah he may build it the usual way.
chunks.st: and during the Sabbatical Year one may even build a wall in his usual manner,
chunks.stMore: as this is not considered an agricultural labor. Consequently, despite the fact that this benefits the garden by offering it protection, it is not prohibited during the Sabbatical Year.

mishnayos.summary: May a Kohen check tzaraas on Chol HaMoed? May a son move his parents' bones to the family grave? And we don't give a hesped close to Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: A Kohen may check tzaraas marks on Chol HaMoed to be lenient,
chunks.explain: He may tell the person he is tahor (pure).
chunks.st: A priest may initially examine an individual showing symptoms of leprosy on the intermediate days of a Festival in order to be lenient,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he may pronounce the individual to be free of leprosy,

words.note: Tzaraas is a skin sickness; a Kohen decides if it makes a person tamei.

chunks.en: but not to be strict.
chunks.explain: He stays quiet instead of calling the person tamei.
chunks.st: but not in order to be stringent;
chunks.stMore: he may not pronounce the individual to be impure. The individual does not become ritually impure until the priest pronounces him to have leprosy, and therefore the priest may remain silent and thereby prevent causing the afflicted individual distress during the Festival.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Not to be lenient and not to be strict.
chunks.st: The priest may not examine the symptoms in order to be lenient or in order to be stringent.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir also said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir also stated
chunks.stMore: another leniency concerning the halakhot of the intermediate days of a Festival:

chunks.en: A person may gather the bones of his father and mother,
chunks.explain: To bury them again in the family grave.
chunks.st: A person may gather the bones of his father and mother from their temporary graves on the intermediate days of a Festival.
chunks.stMore: In ancient times, it was customary to first bury a corpse in a temporary grave. After the flesh had decomposed, the bones would be collected, placed in a coffin, and buried in a vault together with the bones of the deceased individual’s ancestors.

chunks.en: because it is a joy for him.
chunks.st: This is permitted on the intermediate days of a Festival because the fact that one merited to bring the bones of his deceased parents to the graves of their ancestors is a source of joy for him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: It makes him sad, like mourning.
chunks.st: One does not gather these bones on the intermediate days of a Festival, because it is a source of mourning for him.
chunks.stMore: Even though he is happy to be able to bury his parents’ bones in their ancestral graves, he is still pained by the memory of their death.

chunks.en: A person may not stir up crying over a relative who passed away,
chunks.st: And all agree that a person may not arouse [ye’orer]lamentation for his deceased relative,

chunks.en: and may not give a hesped for him,
chunks.st: and he may not eulogize him

words.note: A hesped is a speech about someone who passed away.

chunks.en: in the thirty days before a Yom Tov.
chunks.st: during the thirty days before a pilgrimage Festival.

words.note: Pesach, Shavuos or Sukkos.

mishnayos.stIntro: When symptoms of leprosy appear, they must be examined by a priest, who determines whether or not the symptoms qualify as leprosy.

mishnayos.summary: On Chol HaMoed we may not dig graves ahead of time, but we may prepare what is needed for someone who just passed away.

chunks.en: We may not dig burial spaces or graves on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.explain: To have them ready for later.
chunks.st: One may not dig crypts or graves on the intermediate days of a Festival
chunks.stMore: in preparation for those who are still alive,

words.note: Holes cut into a cave wall for burial.

chunks.en: but we may fix up burial spaces already dug on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.explain: To make one fit for someone who passed away.
chunks.st: but one may adjust previously dug crypts on the intermediate days of a Festival
chunks.stMore: in order to receive a particular corpse.

chunks.en: We may make a pond for washing clothes on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: And one may also construct a laundry pond on the intermediate days of a Festival
chunks.stMore: as it does not involve excessive effort.

words.note: A pool for washing clothes.

chunks.en: and a coffin, when the one who passed away is in the same yard.
chunks.explain: Then everyone knows whom it is for.
chunks.st: And one may also prepare a coffin if he is together with the corpse in the same courtyard,
chunks.stMore: as in that case everyone knows that he is preparing the coffin for the deceased.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah forbids it,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ נְסָרִים:
chunks.en: unless he already has boards with him.
chunks.st: making the coffin unless one has wooden boards with him that had already been cut before the Festival and that need only to be attached.

mishnayos.summary: We don't make weddings on Chol HaMoed, so one joy doesn't mix with the joy of Yom Tov. A woman may still do things to look nice.

chunks.en: We may not get married on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: One may not marry a woman on the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: not a bride marrying for the first time,
chunks.st: not virgins

chunks.en: and not a widow,
chunks.st: and not widows,

chunks.en: and we may not do yibum,
chunks.st: and one may not perform levirate marriage
chunks.stMore: with his sister-in-law, if his brother died childless,

words.note: Marrying the widow of a brother who had no children.

chunks.en: because it is a joy for him.
chunks.explain: We don't mix another joy into the joy of Yom Tov.
chunks.st: because it is a joyous occasion for him.

chunks.en: But a man may remarry his wife whom he had divorced.
chunks.st: However, one may remarry his divorced wife
chunks.stMore: on the intermediate days of a Festival, as this is not as great a joy for him.

chunks.en: A woman may do things to look nice on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: And a woman may engage in all her usual cosmetic treatments to enhance her physical appearance on the intermediate days of a Festival.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: לֹא תָּסוּד מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּוּוּל הוּא לָהּ:
chunks.en: She may not put lime on her skin, because it makes her look bad for a while.
chunks.st: She may not apply lime to her skin because it is temporarily a disgrace to her,
chunks.stMore: as she is unattractive before the lime is peeled off and will therefore be distressed during the Festival.

words.note: A paste spread on the skin that peels off later.

mishnayos.summary: Who may sew on Chol HaMoed and how, and may we fix the cords of a bed?

chunks.en: A regular person may sew the usual way,
chunks.st: A layman, who is not a skilled tailor, may sew in his usual manner if necessary for the Festival,

words.note: Someone who is not a skilled tailor.

chunks.en: but a skilled tailor may only make big, uneven stitches.
chunks.st: whereas a craftsman may form only temporary stitches.

words.note: Big uneven stitches, like a dog's teeth.

chunks.en: We may weave the cords of beds.
chunks.st: And one may interweave the cords attached to the frames of beds upon which a mattress is placed.

words.en: and we may weave cords for

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: We may only tighten the cords.
chunks.st: One may only tighten the cords but not interweave them.

mishnayos.summary: We may set up an oven, a stove and a mill on Chol HaMoed.

chunks.en: We may set up an oven, a stove and a mill on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: One may set up an oven, a stove, and a mill on the intermediate days of a Festival.

words.note: Heavy stones that grind wheat into flour.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: We may not chisel millstones for the first time.
chunks.explain: Roughening them so they grind well.
chunks.st: One may not chisel millstones for the first time on the intermediate days of a Festival.

mishnayos.summary: Simple fixing jobs are allowed on Chol HaMoed: a roof railing, cracks, a broken lock or key. We may also pickle food we can eat on Yom Tov.

chunks.he: עוֹשִׂין מַעֲקֶה לְגַג וּלְמִרְפֶּסֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הֶדְיוֹט,
chunks.en: We may make a railing for a roof or a balcony, the way a regular person would,
chunks.st: One may construct a railing for a roof or a balcony if it is done in a nonprofessional manner, as the work of a layman,

words.note: A low wall around a roof so no one falls.

chunks.en: but not the way an expert builder would.
chunks.st: but not if it is done skillfully, as the work of a craftsman.

chunks.en: We may plaster cracks in an oven
chunks.st: One may plaster the cracks in an oven

chunks.en: and smooth them with a roller
chunks.st: and roll over them with a roller, a wooden tool used to smooth out clay,

chunks.en: by hand or by foot,
chunks.st: with a hand or a foot,

chunks.en: but not with a special pressing tool.
chunks.st: but not with a presser, a tool that is specially designed for this task.

words.note: A special tool made for this job.

chunks.he: הַצִּיר וְהַצִּנּוֹר וְהַקּוֹרָה וְהַמַּנְעוּל וְהַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ,
chunks.en: A door hinge and its socket, the beam, a lock or a key that broke,
chunks.st: With regard to the hinge of a door, and the cylinder of the hinge, and the cross beam that holds the door, and a lock and a key that broke,

words.note: The round hole the hinge turns in.

chunks.en: he may fix them on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: one may fix them on the intermediate days of a Festival
chunks.stMore: as these items are essential for the Festival and their repair cannot be delayed.

chunks.en: as long as he did not plan to save the work for Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: This is permitted, provided that he does not intend ahead of time to do his labor on the Festival
chunks.stMore: and delay it until that time.

chunks.en: And any pickled food
chunks.st: And with regard to all preserved food

chunks.en: that he can eat from on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: from which one can eat on the Festival,
chunks.stMore: since they become ready to be eaten in a short amount of time,

chunks.en: he may pickle them.
chunks.st: he may preserve them on the intermediate days of a Festival.

mishnayos.summary: If something stopped a person from pressing his olives before Yom Tov, may he press them on Chol HaMoed so they don't spoil? Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yosei argue.

chunks.en: Someone who turned over his olives,
chunks.explain: Getting them ready to press for oil.
chunks.st: The mishna discusses one who had already turned over his olives
chunks.stMore: as part of the process of preparing them for pressing,

chunks.en: and then he became an avel, or something else stopped him,
chunks.explain: An avel is a mourner, who may not work.
chunks.st: and mourning for a close relative befell him and as a result he was prohibited from engaging in work, or some other unavoidable accident occurred,

chunks.en: or his workers fooled him,
chunks.explain: They promised to come but did not.
chunks.st: or his workers misled him,
chunks.stMore: promising to come but failing to do so, so that he could not press his olives before the Festival.

chunks.he: טוֹעֵן קוֹרָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וּמַנִּיחָהּ לְאַחַר הַמּוֹעֵד.
chunks.en: he may put the heavy beam on the olives one time and leave it until after Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The weight squeezes out some oil so the olives don't spoil.
chunks.st: Under these circumstances, during the intermediate days of the Festival, he may place the olives in the press and load the beam with weights for the initial pressing of the olives and leave it this way until after the Festival;

words.note: A heavy log in the olive press that squeezes out the oil.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: He may press the olives, finish the job, and close up the barrels the usual way.
chunks.st: He may press the olives and complete the process and then plug each barrel of oil in its usual manner.
chunks.stMore: Since delay can entail financial loss, the Sages did not require him to alter the normal process of extracting the oil.

mishnayos.summary: The same question about wine that is waiting in the pit: may he finish taking it out on Chol HaMoed so it won't turn sour?

chunks.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה יֵינוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר
chunks.en: And also someone whose wine was in the pit,
chunks.explain: The pit next to the winepress that collects the wine.
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to one whose wine was already in the collection pit beside the wine press and needed to be removed lest it sour,

chunks.en: and he became an avel, or something else stopped him,
chunks.st: and mourning for some close relative or some other unavoidable accident befell him,

chunks.en: or his workers fooled him,
chunks.st: or his workers misled him,
chunks.stMore: promising to come but failing to do so,

chunks.en: he may draw off the wine, finish, and close up the barrels the usual way.
chunks.st: during the intermediate days of the Festival he may draw off the wine and complete the process, and then plug each barrel of wine in its usual manner;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yosei says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He should make a wooden cover for the pit,
chunks.st: He should construct a wooden panel to cover the collection pit

chunks.en: so the wine won't turn sour.
chunks.st: so that the wine will not sour.

mishnayos.summary: A person may do work on Chol HaMoed to stop a loss, but not if he planned ahead to leave the work for Chol HaMoed.

chunks.en: A person may bring his fruit in from the field because of thieves,
chunks.st: A person may bring his fruit in from the field on the intermediate days of the Festival because he is concerned about thieves,

chunks.en: and take his flax out of the soaking pool
chunks.st: and he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool

words.note: A plant used to make linen.

chunks.en: so it won't be ruined,
chunks.st: so that it is not ruined from soaking too long in the water,

chunks.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּן אֶת מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַמּוֹעֵד.
chunks.en: as long as he did not plan to do his work on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: provided that he does not plan from the outset to perform his work on the intermediate days of the Festival.

chunks.he: וְכֻלָּן אִם כִּוְּנוּ מְלַאכְתָּן בַּמּוֹעֵד, יֹאבֵדוּ:
chunks.en: In all these cases, if they planned their work for Chol HaMoed, what they made must be lost.
chunks.explain: They may not get any benefit from it.
chunks.st: And with regard to all of these cases, if one planned from the outset to perform his labor on the intermediate days of the Festival, the fruit of that labor must be lost
chunks.stMore: and no benefit may be derived from it.

mishnayos.summary: On Chol HaMoed we don't buy houses or animals or move house, unless it is needed for Yom Tov or to stop a loss.

chunks.en: We may not buy houses,
chunks.st: One may not purchase houses,

chunks.en: servants or animals,
chunks.st: slaves, and cattle on the intermediate days of a Festival

chunks.en: unless it is needed for Yom Tov,
chunks.st: unless it is for the sake of the Festival,

chunks.en: or the seller needs the money,
chunks.st: or to provide for the needs of the seller

chunks.en: because he has nothing to eat.
chunks.st: who does not have anything to eat.

chunks.en: We may not move our things from one house to another,
chunks.st: One may not move his possessions from house to house during the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: but he may move them into his yard.
chunks.st: but he may move them to his courtyard if that is necessary.

chunks.en: We may not bring things home from a craftsman's shop.
chunks.st: One may not bring home utensils from the house of a craftsman after he has completed his work,

chunks.en: But if he is worried about them,
chunks.explain: That they might be stolen.
chunks.st: but if one is concerned about them that if he leaves them in the craftsman’s house they are likely to be stolen,

chunks.en: he may move them to another yard.
chunks.st: he may move them to another courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: We may protect drying figs, and sellers and workers may quietly do what is needed for Yom Tov.

chunks.en: We may cover drying figs with straw.
chunks.st: On the intermediate days of a Festival, figs that were spread out to dry may be covered with straw
chunks.stMore: to protect them from rain and dew.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: We may even pile them up thick.
chunks.explain: So the top figs protect the ones below.
chunks.st: One may even condense the figs.

chunks.en: People who sell fruit,
chunks.st: Those who sell produce,

chunks.en: clothing and utensils
chunks.st: clothing, and utensils

chunks.en: may sell quietly, for what is needed for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: may sell them in private, for the sake of the Festival.

chunks.en: Fishermen, people who crush grain, and people who pound beans
chunks.st: Fishermen, and groats makers [dashoshot], and bean pounders, who pulverize the beans,

chunks.en: may work quietly, for what is needed for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: may ply their trades in private for the sake of the Festival.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: They were strict with themselves.
chunks.explain: They did not do this work even for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: They were stringent with themselves
chunks.stMore: to refrain from this work even with respect to what was needed for the Festival.

mishnayos.summary: Usually we may not get a haircut on Chol HaMoed. This mishnah lists people who could not cut their hair before Yom Tov, so they may cut it on Chol HaMoed.

chunks.en: These people may get a haircut on Chol HaMoed:
chunks.st: And these may shave and cut their hair on the intermediate days of a Festival:

chunks.en: someone who comes back from overseas,
chunks.st: One who comes from a country overseas;

chunks.en: and someone set free from captivity,
chunks.st: and one who is released from a house of captivity;

chunks.en: someone who comes out of prison,
chunks.st: and one who comes out of prison on the intermediate days of a Festival;

chunks.en: someone in nidui, when the Sages lift it,
chunks.explain: Nidui is a punishment; during it he may not cut his hair.
chunks.st: and one who had been ostracized and therefore prohibited from cutting his hair, and the Sages released him from his decree of ostracism on the intermediate days of the Festival;

words.note: Someone the beis din pushed away as a punishment.

chunks.en: and someone who asked a Sage to undo his neder and was released,
chunks.explain: He had promised not to cut his hair.
chunks.st: and similarly, one who had vowed not to cut his hair and then requested of a Sage to dissolve his vow and was released from it on the intermediate days of the Festival;

chunks.en: a nazir whose time just ended,
chunks.st: and the nazirite whose term of naziriteship ended on the intermediate days of a Festival;

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair for a time.

chunks.en: and a metzora going from tamei to tahor.
chunks.explain: He must shave to become tahor.
chunks.st: and the leper who needs to purify himself on the intermediate days and must shave his entire body in order to leave his state of ritual impurity and regain his ritual purity.
chunks.stMore: Since these people were not able to cut their hair on the eve of the Festival, they are permitted to do so on the intermediate days of the Festival.

words.note: Someone who had tzaraas.

mishnayos.summary: Usually we may not wash clothes on Chol HaMoed. This mishnah lists who may, and which towels may be washed.

chunks.en: These people may wash clothes on Chol HaMoed:
someone who comes back from overseas,
and someone set free from captivity,
someone who comes out of prison,
someone in nidui, when the Sages lift it,

words.note: Someone the beis din pushed away as a punishment.

chunks.en: and someone who asked a Sage to undo his neder and was released.
chunks.explain: He had promised not to wash his clothes.

chunks.he: מִטְפְּחוֹת הַיָּדַיִם וּמִטְפְּחוֹת הַסַּפָּרִים וּמִטְפְּחוֹת הַסְּפָג,
chunks.en: Hand towels, barbers' sheets and drying towels may be washed,
chunks.explain: They get dirty quickly.

chunks.en: Zavim, zavos, women who are niddah, and women who just had a baby,
chunks.explain: These are kinds of tumah; washing clothes helps them become tahor.

words.note: Men with a kind of tumah.
Women with a kind of tumah.
Another kind of tumah.

chunks.en: and everyone going from tamei to tahor:
these are allowed.
But everyone else may not.

mishnayos.summary: These important papers may be written on Chol HaMoed, because waiting could cause a loss.

chunks.en: These may be written on Chol HaMoed:
chunks.st: And these are the documents that may be written on the intermediate days of a Festival:

chunks.en: papers for kiddushin, the first step of marriage,
chunks.st: Documents of betrothal of wives, through which bridegrooms betroth their brides;

words.note: The first step of getting married.

chunks.en: a get, and receipts,
chunks.st: bills of divorce; receipts for the repayment of debts;

words.note: A get is a paper of divorce.
A paper that says a loan was paid back.

chunks.en: a will, a gift paper, and a pruzbul,
chunks.st: wills [deyateiki]; deeds of gift; perozbolin,
chunks.stMore: documents through which lenders authorize the courts to collect their loans on their behalf, thereby preventing the Sabbatical year from canceling their debts;

words.note: A paper giving away a person's things.
A paper that keeps Shemittah from canceling a loan.

chunks.en: papers that value land, and papers promising to feed someone,
chunks.st: letters of valuation, which were drawn up by the court when they valuated property and transferred it to the lender; and letters of sustenance,
chunks.stMore: which were drawn up when one accepted upon himself to maintain another, e.g., his step-daughter.

words.note: When beis din sets what land is worth, to pay a debt.
A promise to feed someone, like a stepdaughter.

chunks.en: papers of chalitzah and of mi'un,
chunks.explain: Papers that free a woman from a marriage bond.
chunks.st: The list continues: Documents of the ritual through which the brother-in-law frees the yevama of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza],
chunks.stMore: thereby freeing her from the obligation to marry one of her deceased husband’s brothers; documents in which the court records the refusal of a girl upon reaching majority to remain married to the man to whom her mother or brothers married her as a minor after the death of her father;

words.note: Done instead of yibum; it frees a brother's widow.
When a young girl refuses a marriage made for her.

chunks.en: papers about settling an argument,
chunks.st: documents of arbitration, in which the court summarizes a conflict that had been resolved through arbitration;

words.note: Settling an argument through chosen judges.

chunks.en: rulings of beis din,
chunks.st: court rulings;

chunks.en: and letters of the government.
chunks.st: and the official correspondence of the ruling authorities.

mishnayos.summary: We don't write loan papers, sifrei Torah, tefillin or mezuzos on Chol HaMoed, unless there is a real need.

chunks.en: We may not write loan papers on Chol HaMoed.
chunks.st: One may not write bills of debt on the intermediate days of a Festival.

chunks.en: But if the lender does not trust the borrower,
chunks.st: But if the lender does not trust the borrower, and he is concerned that the borrower will later deny the loan,

chunks.en: or the scribe has nothing to eat,
chunks.st: or if the scribe has nothing to eat,

chunks.en: then he may write it.
chunks.st: then he may write a bill of debt during the Festival week.

chunks.en: We may not write sifrei Torah,
chunks.st: One may not write Torah scrolls,

chunks.en: tefillin or mezuzos
chunks.st: phylacteries, or mezuzot

chunks.en: on Chol HaMoed, and we may not fix even one letter,
chunks.st: on the intermediate days of a Festival, nor may one correct a single letter,

chunks.en: even in the Sefer Torah of Ezra.
chunks.explain: A special Sefer Torah kept in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: even in the Torah scroll of Ezra,
chunks.stMore: which was kept in the Temple and upon which all the Jewish communities relied.

words.note: Another version: the Azarah, the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: A person may write tefillin and mezuzos for himself,
chunks.st: One may write phylacteries and mezuzot for himself
chunks.stMore: on the intermediate days of a Festival if he needs them.

chunks.en: and spin techeiles wool on his leg for his tzitzis.
chunks.explain: Not the usual way, with a spindle.
chunks.st: And one may spin sky-blue wool for his ritual fringes on his thigh,
chunks.stMore: but not in the ordinary manner with a spindle, as this procedure must be performed in an altered manner on the intermediate days of a Festival.

words.note: Sky-blue wool for tzitzis.

mishnayos.summary: When someone starts mourning before Yom Tov, Yom Tov cuts the mourning short. Shabbos is different.

chunks.en: Someone who buries his relative
chunks.st: One who buries his deceased relative

chunks.en: three days before a Yom Tov:
chunks.st: three days before a pilgrimage Festival

chunks.en: the seven days of mourning are canceled for him.
chunks.explain: Yom Tov ends his shivah.
chunks.st: has the decree of the seven-day period of mourning, i.e., the halakhot and prohibitions associated with that period, nullified for him by the Festival.
chunks.stMore: He is not required to complete this seven-day mourning period after the Festival.

words.note: The first seven days of mourning.

chunks.en: If it was eight days before, the thirty days of mourning are canceled,
chunks.st: If one buries his deceased relative eight days before a pilgrimage Festival, then the decree of thirty days is nullified for him.
chunks.stMore: The restrictions that ordinarily apply during this thirty-day mourning period no longer apply after the Festival.

words.note: Thirty days of lighter mourning.

chunks.en: because they said,
chunks.st: This is because the Sages said a principle with regard to this issue:

chunks.en: Shabbos counts, and does not stop the mourning;
chunks.explain: Shabbos is one of the seven days, and mourning goes on after it.
chunks.st: Shabbat counts as one of the days of mourning, although one may not mourn on it and it does not interrupt
chunks.stMore: the mourning period, which continues after Shabbat.

chunks.en: the Yamim Tovim stop the mourning,
chunks.st: The pilgrimage Festivals, on the other hand, interrupt
chunks.stMore: the mourning period, so that if one began mourning before such a Festival, then the mourning period is canceled by the Festival.

chunks.en: but they do not count.
chunks.explain: Days of Yom Tov are not counted as mourning days.
chunks.st: They do not, however, count.
chunks.stMore: If one did not begin mourning before the Festival, or if his relative died during the Festival, then he is required to complete his mourning period afterward, as the days of the Festival do not count toward the requisite days of mourning.

mishnayos.summary: For mourning, which special days are like Shabbos and which are like the Yamim Tovim?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: Since the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: From the time that the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: Shavuos is like Shabbos.
chunks.explain: For mourning, it counts but does not stop the mourning.
chunks.st: Shavuot is like Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: because nowadays the days following Shavuot are not treated like Festival days. When the Temple stood, many of the Festival’s offerings that could not be sacrificed on Shavuot itself would be sacrificed during the six days following the Festival. Nowadays, however, when offerings are no longer sacrificed, Shavuot lasts for only one day in Eretz Yisrael, and therefore it is treated like Shabbat with regard to mourning: It counts as one of the days of mourning, but does not interrupt the period of mourning.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur
chunks.st: Even Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur

chunks.en: are like the Yamim Tovim.
chunks.st: are considered like the pilgrimage Festivals, in that they interrupt the mourning period but are not counted toward the days of mourning.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: Not like this one, and not like that one.
chunks.st: The halakha is neither in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Eliezer nor in accordance with the statement of Rabban Gamliel.

chunks.en: Rather, Shavuos is like the other Yamim Tovim,
chunks.st: Rather, with regard to mourning, Shavuot is treated like the other pilgrimage Festivals,

chunks.en: and Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur are like Shabbos.
chunks.st: whereas Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur are treated like Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: Some mourning practices are not done on Chol HaMoed, but we may still comfort the mourners.

chunks.en: On Chol HaMoed we do not tear our clothes in mourning,
chunks.st: Mourners do not rend their garments during the intermediate days of a Festival

chunks.en: or uncover the shoulder,
chunks.st: and do not remove their garments from their shoulders.

chunks.en: and we do not bring the mourner's first meal,
chunks.st: And others do not provide them with a meal [mavrin] after the burial,

words.note: The first meal after a burial, brought by others.

chunks.en: except for close relatives of the one who passed away.
chunks.st: except for close relatives of the deceased.

chunks.he: וְאֵין מַבְרִין אֶלָּא עַל מִטָּה זְקוּפָה.
chunks.en: And we give that meal only on a bed standing upright.
chunks.explain: Not on a bed that is turned over.
chunks.st: And the consolers provide the first meal after the burial only while the mourner is sitting on an upright bed, and not on one that is overturned.

chunks.en: We do not bring the food to the house of mourning
chunks.st: One does not bring the first meal after the burial to the house of mourning

chunks.he: לֹא בְּטַבְלָא וְלֹא בְאִסְקוּטְלָא וְלֹא בְקָנוֹן,
chunks.en: on a tray, in a bowl, or in a narrow basket,
chunks.st: on a small tray [tavla], in a bowl [iskutla], or in a narrow-mouthed basket [kanon],

chunks.en: but in plain baskets.
chunks.st: but rather in ordinary baskets.

chunks.en: We do not say the mourners' bracha on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: And the mourners’ blessing is not recited on the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: but people may stand in a row and comfort them,
chunks.st: but the consolers may stand in a row when the mourners leave the cemetery and console them.

chunks.en: and the mourners send the many people home.
chunks.st: And the mourners dismiss the many consolers, by telling them that they may return home after they have fulfilled the mitzva of consoling the mourners.

mishnayos.summary: On Chol HaMoed we keep mourning quieter: the bier is not set down in the street, and women may cry out but not clap.

chunks.en: We do not put the bier down in the street,

words.note: The bed on which someone who passed away is carried.

chunks.en: so people won't start giving hespeds.
And a woman's bier is never put down,
out of respect for her.
On Chol HaMoed women may cry out together,
but may not clap their hands in sadness.
Rabbi Yishmael says,
Those close to the bier may clap.

mishnayos.summary: How women mourn on Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah and Purim. The mishnah ends with a promise: in the future Hashem will end death and wipe away every tear.

chunks.en: On Rosh Chodesh,
chunks.st: On New Moons,

chunks.en: Chanukah and Purim,
chunks.st: Hanukkah and Purim, which are not Festivals by Torah law,

chunks.en: women may cry out together and clap.
chunks.st: the women may both wail and clap their hands in mourning.

chunks.en: But on both kinds of days, they may not say a kinah.
chunks.st: On both the intermediate days of a Festival and on New Moons, Hanukkah and Purim they may not lament.

words.note: A sad song for someone who passed away.

chunks.en: Once the person has been buried,
chunks.st: After the deceased has been buried

chunks.en: they may not cry out or clap.
chunks.st: they may neither wail nor clap.

chunks.en: What is crying out together?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: What is considered wailing?

chunks.en: When they all cry out at the same time.
chunks.st: This is when they all wail together simultaneously.

chunks.he: קִינָה, שֶׁאַחַת מְדַבֶּרֶת וְכֻלָּן עוֹנוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ,
chunks.en: A kinah is when one woman speaks and they all answer after her,
chunks.st: And what is considered a lament? This is when one speaks and they all answer after her with a repeated refrain,

chunks.en: as it says (Yirmiyahu 9):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: Teach your daughters to cry,
chunks.st: “And teach your daughters wailing

chunks.en: and each woman, her friend a kinah.
chunks.st: and everyone her neighbor lamentation” (Jeremiah 9:19).
chunks.stMore: In order to conclude on a positive note, the mishna says:

chunks.en: But about the time to come,
chunks.st: But with regard to the future,

chunks.en: it says (Yeshayahu 25):
chunks.st: the verse states:

chunks.en: He will end death forever,
chunks.st: “He will destroy death forever;

chunks.en: and Hashem will wipe away tears
chunks.st: and the Lord, God, will wipe away tears

chunks.en: from every face.
chunks.st: from off all faces and the reproach of His people He will take away from off all the earth” (Isaiah 25:8).
